title: Gegenpressing (Counter-Press After Losing Possession)
content: Gegenpressing is an immediate, high-intensity collective press to win the ball back within 5–8 seconds of losing possession. The principle: in the first moments after losing the ball, the opponent is disorganised, ball-focused, and hasn't yet established their positional structure — this is the optimal moment to press and win the ball back in a dangerous position. All nearby players collapse on the ball carrier immediately, with the priority of stopping a counter-attack first and winning the ball back second. The press must be triggered automatically by any player losing the ball, not by a coach instruction. Key: nearby players must press from multiple angles simultaneously to eliminate passing options, not one at a time. Effectiveness falls off sharply after 6 seconds as the opponent has time to move the ball away from pressure.
example_questions: What should the team do immediately after we lose the ball in the opponent's half?
We just gave the ball away and the opponent is trying to build a counter-attack, so how do we win it back quickly?
As a forward, what is my specific job in the first few seconds after my teammate loses possession?
We often lose the ball and then have to chase it back down the pitch, so how can we stop that from happening?
